title: Command Injection via child_process.exec
platform_conditions: Node.js runtime (child_process module); shell resolution is /bin/sh on POSIX and cmd.exe on Windows
security_mechanism: child_process.exec and execSync do not take an argv vector: they hand the whole string to a shell, so metacharacters in interpolated input (';', '|', '&', '$( )', backquotes, newlines) end the intended command and start attacker-chosen ones. spawn with shell:true rebuilds the same string form. Even with the argv form, an input value that starts with '-' is consumed by the spawned program as an option (argument injection), which for utilities like curl or tar can flip them into file-write or exfiltration primitives.

source_sink_clues.source: Hosts, URLs, filenames, or free-text fields from requests that are interpolated into a command string or passed as leading argv elements.
source_sink_clues.sink: child_process.exec / execSync with template strings; spawn / execFile with shell:true; argv elements starting with '-' taken from input

tracking_guards: Prefer execFile/spawn with an argv array, shell unset, and the dynamic value as one element; verify '--' is placed before attacker-derived arguments; verify strict allowlist validation (e.g. hostname grammar) before interpolation into any shell string.
not_candidate_when: The command is a fixed constant with no interpolation, the dynamic value lands in a single argv element after a literal '--' and the utility takes no further options, or the value is validated against a strict grammar that excludes shell metacharacters.
public_references: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html
